_comment: WhatsApp Flow for multi-answer (select-all-that-apply) training quiz questions.
_instructions: 1. Registered automatically by `npm run setup:flows` (flow-configs.js → 'Training Multi-Answer Question').
2. The resulting Flow ID is written to TRAINING_MSQ_FLOW_ID in your .env.
4. ONE Flow serves EVERY multi-answer question: the question text, the option list and the
already-selected set are all supplied dynamically by the endpoint's INIT. There are no
per-option slots and no per-question Flow.
5. Leaving TRAINING_MSQ_FLOW_ID unset is the rollback lever — delivery falls back to the
interactive-list + Done path with no deploy.
6. Modelled on attendance-marking-flow.json (the proven dynamic-data CheckboxGroup pattern here).
_notes: bd-43496 — TWO controls, one screen. A CheckboxGroup CANNOT ask for exactly one answer: Meta
enforces `max-selected-items >= 2` (MINIMUM_VALUE_REQUIRED). Because our value is data-bound,
the JSON still uploads clean and the floor is enforced ON THE DEVICE at render time — the right
screen paints for a split second, then 'Something Went Wrong', while the endpoint logs a
perfectly normal INIT. So single-answer questions (which reach this Flow when their interactive
list rendering would exceed the 1024-char body cap) use a RadioButtonsGroup, which has no
min/max properties and is single-select by construction. `is_multi`/`is_single` gate visibility;
exactly one of the two is ever shown. Both are `required: false` — a hidden required field
blocks submission — so emptiness is rejected server-side instead (handleQuizFlowSubmission
re-sends the question when nothing valid arrives).
Option ids are the question's CANONICAL 1-based option indices, never display positions —
the endpoint orders the list per the attempt's seeded shuffle but the id always identifies
the option the database knows, so the stored answer stays comparable with every historical row.
init-values pre-checks a partially-answered question. Init-values only apply reliably once the
Flow is PUBLISHED; on a DRAFT the boxes may render unchecked.
The Footer completes the Flow rather than calling data_exchange: the selection is a single
atomic submission, so there is nothing to round-trip and no ~10s endpoint budget to respect.

question_text.__example__: Which of these are formative assessment techniques?
